searchText: OK, seems it does mean that the block is not yet fully validated. Let me know if I'm wrong. `valid` is an optional field to indicate if it's valid (no exception) during the `on_block` call; if not specified, it is true by default. (https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/tree/dev/tests/formats/fork_choice#on_block-execution-step) hm... "If it's `false`, this execution step is expected to be invalid." this should mean that the block is permanently invalid. That's the opposite to my assumption "OK, seems it does mean that the block is not yet fully validated". https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/tests/core/pyspec/eth2spec/test/helpers/fork_choice.py#L201 - "is not valid" seems is either optimistic either invalid. I'm again confused. We use the same helper for both basic FC and optimistic sync tests 😅 In optimistic sync tests, `valid` should be determined by `payloadStatus`. (https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/tree/dev/tests/formats/fork_choice#on_payload_info-execution-step) OK, so the meaning of `valid` is different in basic FC and optimistic sync tests? If yes, then I must say it's not ideal 🙂
